neighbours.label: a warning on how to treat a claim or a risk (treated with caution, with a grain of salt, at your own risk, at face value), as opposed to the same verbs in plain use
fire: The sample is small and so should be read with caution.
That rumor should be taken with a pinch of salt.
They may not be safe, so try them at your own risk.
Enter the cave at your own risk.
His claims should not be taken at face value.
Treat these numbers with some skepticism.
Polls this early must be viewed with care.
Readers should take this story with a grain of salt.
quiet: The sample is small and so should be mailed by Friday.
That rug should be taken to the back room.
They may not be open, so try them on Monday.
Enter the hall by the side door.
His bags should not be left on the bus.
Add these numbers with a calculator.
Plants this early must be kept in the shed.
Readers should read this story to their kids.

short: take with caution, at your own risk
